newsitem.title: IRAN: Former Iranian rebel wants to run for president.
newsitem.headline: Former Iranian rebel wants to run for president.

text.p: A former member of an Iraq-based Iranian rebel group said on Thursday he had returned home to run in presidential elections in May on an anti-violence platform.

Ali Farasati, 40, told reporters he came back to Iran last week after a self-imposed exile since 1980 in Iraq and France during which time he said he had been an active member of the Mujahideen Khalq armed opposition group.
Farasati said he left the group six years ago and was given a passport by Iran's embassy in Paris recently to return while his wife and child remained in France.
"My election slogan is: 'Boycott violence'. I think there has been a development in which the advocates of violence are isolated both in the opposition and in the government," he said.
Registration of candidates for the May 23 polls to elect a successor to President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani through 2001 has not yet started.
Candidates will be screened by the Guardian Council, a body of lawyers and Shi'ite Moslem clerics which in past elections disqualified all but a handful of those who signed up.
Farasati is the sixth person to announce his intention to run. Parliament Speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri appears to be the leading candidate after keeping a high profile in the media in the past year.
Tehran has blamed the Mujahideen, whose forces have been involved in several clashes with state troops in the past few weeks, for bombings and attacks across the Iran-Iraq border.
The group denies attacking civilians but has taken responsibility for hitting military, government and economic targets.
